requirements.requirement: Run a functioning web application on node1 inside a chroot as the unprivileged account appsvc, serving on port 8080.
requirements.summary: Direct process evidence shows Python running with UID/GID 992 as appsvc, process root /srv/app-chroot, no effective/permitted/ambient capabilities, and a listener on 0.0.0.0:8080. Both the health endpoint and application page returned HTTP 200 before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Start the application automatically at boot without requiring an interactive login session.
requirements.summary: The unit was enabled and healthy before reboot. A bounded reboot changed the boot identity, after which the current-boot journal recorded automatic service startup, the service was active, and HTTP responses succeeded. appsvc uses nologin and no appsvc login session was present.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with that platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 across the work and reboot. The application uses the already installed RHEL Python 3.12.9 runtime copied into the chroot; final package health remained successful.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The captured restart protocol is complete for node1: it includes a healthy pre-restart state, scheduled-reboot acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, application checksum, HTTP behavior, firewall, SELinux, and system state. Final operation is healthy, though several reverted troubleshooting mutations and a few retained unused chroot directories reduce operational-hygiene quality.
limitations: The lifecycle snapshots do not inventory the chroot contents, account definition, or systemd unit, so those aspects rely on direct executor command evidence.

No package transaction history was captured; platform preservation is supported by identical before/after release and kernel observations, use of the installed Python runtime, the complete command timeline, and a healthy final package-manager check.

The provenance of final chroot directories such as sys, root, and var is not established precisely enough to classify them as unnecessary mutations; only directories directly tied to captured mutation commands were penalized.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final hygiene was generally healthy: no failed units, package damage, SELinux weakening, or unrelated listener remained, and the requested service survived reboot. Several bounded troubleshooting mutations did not contribute to the final implementation: cmd-2a6c9406d19e4a3a created chroot run/dev/proc/tmp paths; the run subtree was later removed by cmd-bc3cbe9895e14219, while empty dev/proc/tmp directories remained. cmd-d418f70d418c4b12 created a dummy journal dev-log file, replaced by the socket experiment in cmd-1fcc508902594287 and ultimately removed by cmd-301d6f0709bc4b31. cmd-db069bfb5b30431c temporarily weakened ProtectSystem from strict to full, and cmd-7caf82125e554b9d temporarily suppressed stdout/stderr; both changes were reverted by cmd-a2fbe6e10e574367. cmd-301d6f0709bc4b31 temporarily changed ownership and mode of the journal directory, which was subsequently removed by cmd-bc3cbe9895e14219. These were low-risk and mostly fully restored, but the retained unused directories and repeated failed-service experiments warrant a moderate hygiene deduction.
